topicName: Database Testing & Basic SQL Queries for Testers
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Database Testing & Basic SQL Queries for Testers"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As a manual tester, verifying the graphical user interface is only half the battle. Behind almost every modern application lies a relational database. Database testing ensures that data integrity, consistency, and security are maintained throughout application workflows."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Database Testing Matters"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Integrity: Ensures that the data saved via the UI matches the data stored in the database backend."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Accuracy: Validates calculations, default values, and formatting applied before persistence."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Business Rule Enforcement: Verifies that constraints like foreign keys, primary keys, and unique checks work as expected."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Essential SQL Commands for Testers"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Structured Query Language (SQL) is used to communicate with databases. As a manual tester, you will primarily use Data Retrieval Language (DRL) commands to query data."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The SELECT Statement"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The SELECT statement is used to fetch data from a database. You can retrieve specific columns or all columns using the asterisk (*) wildcard."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT first_name, last_name FROM users;"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"2. The WHERE Clause"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The WHERE clause filters records based on specific conditions. This is vital when testing specific user actions or looking for precise records."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'Completed';"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Using AND, OR, and NOT Operators"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can combine multiple conditions using logical operators to narrow down your test results."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' AND price < 500;"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"4. The ORDER BY Clause"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"The ORDER BY keyword sorts the result set in ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC) order, which is helpful when verifying sorting features on the UI."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM customers ORDER BY signup_date DESC;"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Database Testing in Manual QA"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always test negative scenarios, such as inserting duplicate emails or null values into mandatory fields."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Perform end-to-end data validation: create a record in the UI, then immediately write a SELECT query to confirm the exact values hit the database."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Never run DELETE or UPDATE queries on production or shared staging environments without proper authorization and backups."}]
